topic.title: The Deep-Sea Creatures That Glow in the Dark

script.full_text: Descend past a thousand meters and the sunlight vanishes completely. Yet this crushing darkness is the most lit-up place on Earth, where nine out of ten animals make their own light. It is a chemical trick called bioluminescence. A molecule named luciferin reacts with oxygen, and the energy escapes not as heat, but as cold living light, glowing blue-green through the deep. Every glow has a purpose. Anglerfish dangle a lure to trap prey. Others flash to find a mate, or erase their own shadow from below in a vanishing act called counter-illumination. By borrowing these very molecules, scientists now light up living cells, track diseases, and watch tumors grow. The deep sea's quiet glow is quietly rewriting modern medicine.
